name: Serpentine
beta: Head up and leftward, clipping three bolts (Revelation shares the third), then from there trend up and rightward to a stance for the belay. Next go straight up and then rightward again to the following belay; three pitches in all.
overview: Slants upward and leftward over three bolts, the last of them common with Revelation, then turns up and rightward to a belay; the rest goes straight up, then right again.

current.location: by a big oak at the wall right-hand end

name: Shave Your Bump
beta: Climb the biggest slab; the only bolt comes high up.
overview: A slab route on the largest slab of its crag, carrying just one bolt close to the finish.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: largest slab on a small crag partway along the drive in

name: Shell Shock
beta: Clip the opening bolt from a stick. The boulder-problem crux sits right at the base; once past it you step onto terrain that is less steep.
overview: A bolted overhang line. The hard part: boulder-problem start, then easing off. Clip 6 bolts on the way up.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.anchor: 2-bolt anchor also used by Sunnyside Up

name: Ship of Fools
beta: Climb a crack system that goes straight up beside a cave; a single bolt sits roughly thirty feet off the ground.
overview: A direct crack line beside a cave, with one bolt roughly 30 ft above the ground.

current.area_walk_in: From Hidden Valley campground walk north, past the Iron Door Cave area and the east end of The Blob, then aim for the overhanging face across easy boulders to a mostly flat base.

name: Shongo Pavi
beta: Begin fifteen feet beyond Jedi Master, then climb a crack that trends up-left beside a little bush, moving onto the face to clip a single bolt.
overview: A crack heading up and leftward beside a little shrub, then face with a bolt.

name: Short Term Memory
beta: Pull through the crimps to the second bolt, work the thin reachy sequence above it, then continue to the top.
overview: A crimpy face route with a thin, reachy section just above the second clip.

name: Sign Language
beta: Eight bolts lead up the northwest arete above the water. The loose rock on the line's right has largely gone over the years.
overview: A bolted arete line (runs the arete on the northwest corner overlooking the ocean). Clip 8 bolts on the way up.

name: Silent but Deadly
beta: Follow the right-hand bolt line; how hard it feels depends on how closely you stay with the bolts.
overview: The right-hand one of two steep bolt lines on a brown wall of buckets; how hard it feels hinges on how faithfully you follow the bolts.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Silent Scream (aka Shock the Monkey)

overview: The left-hand of two steep bolt lines on a brown wall full of buckets.

name: Six-Gun by My Side
beta: Five bolts lead to the shared anchors, though clip one can easily be skipped.
overview: A five-bolt line that ends at the anchors shared with its neighbour. The lowest bolt is easy to skip.

current.area_walk_in: The trail reaches the wall at its right end, so you meet the routes in the reverse of their listed left-to-right order.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Sleek Beak
beta: Three bolts lead up the north face; after the third, trend leftward and upward to join a neighboring route at its lone bolt.
overview: Three bolts; from the last, step diagonally leftward to a neighbouring line's lone bolt.

name: Smash n Grab
beta: A rappel anchor partway up the line means a single rope is enough to get down.
overview: A newer, long bolted line starting between the arete on its left and the crack to its right.

current.area_walk_in: Head up the fire road past the cliff, then take the narrow trail that doubles back through manzanita; allow 20 to 45 minutes from the road.

current.location: right of the arete and left of the crack

name: Little Big Dog
beta: Pull through the undercut on its leftmost edge to a bolt, then angle rightward for the next bolt, which sits at the shoulder; keep going to the top. The first clip is a long reach and the start holds the crux; a variation starting beyond the undercut's leftmost end is slightly easier.
overview: Climbs along the undercut's lefthand edge to a bolt, then angles rightward to another bolt set on the shoulder, then continues to the summit. The big distance up to bolt number one makes the opening the crux; going around the undercut's far side reaches that bolt at the lower grade.

current.area_walk_in: A 30-ft boulder standing 50 ft uphill of Toog's, beside the official central access path to The Balconies. The routes are on its uphill side, looking toward The Balconies.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: No Smiles
beta: A bold lead that pulls over the undercut near its right-hand end, with two bolts along the way.
overview: A committing lead over the bulge, going over the undercut's righthand end with two bolts for protection.

current.area_walk_in: A 30-ft boulder standing 50 ft uphill of Toog's, beside the official central access path to The Balconies. The routes are on its uphill side, looking toward The Balconies.

name: Smokestack Lightning
beta: Begin beneath a chockstone and work the cracks leftward, clipping a couple of bolts close to the top.
overview: A crack line fronting the tallest rock, finishing past a pair of bolts.

current.area_walk_in: Strike out northwest over a wide level expanse and a large wash; the biggest, tallest rock of the group is around three-quarters of a mile away.

name: Solar Power
beta: Fun, pocketed climbing, with one slightly committing stretch in the gap separating bolts three and four.
overview: A pocketed face route that is enjoyable but slightly serious in the last stretch, where the clips spread out.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Song of the Siren
beta: Step off the round boulder, clip the lone bolt, and complete the climb in the leftward-leaning groove; gear up to about 6 inches is useful.
overview: A line that starts from a round boulder and ends in a groove that leans leftward, with a single bolt low on the route.

current.area_walk_in: Take the nature trail northeast, crest a rise and pass a marker, then after roughly 100 yards swing left over flat slabs and head southwest into a brushy, boulder-strewn valley. Where it opens (Lost Corridor) bear right into a tighter passage that pinches very narrow; when it widens, the Corridor Face is the wall on your left. A more direct option starts below the Pathetic routes and heads northeast via a rocky passage.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: launching from a rounded boulder above and to the right of Fool's Gold

name: South Face
beta: Pitch one scoots over a short apron, clipping a trio of bolts plus a pin hammered into a flake, to a ledge beneath a long arching corner system. Above, a string of bolts forms a ladder that looks never to have been completed.
overview: An unfinished line. Pitch one crosses a 40-ft apron to a ledge under a long, curving corner; it is crumbly here and there but rewarding. Pitch two is a bolt ladder that appears abandoned, ending at a pair of doubled bolts.

current.anchor: bolt belay at the right end of the ledge, or a slung chock at the left end

name: Southwest Passage
beta: Begin behind a boulder and take the leftmost fissure, trending leftward to Bat Ledge. Pitch two drifts leftward, nearly brushing a neighboring line, then returns rightward to meet another route where it has a bolt.
overview: Pitch one is a crack that angles leftward to Bat Ledge; pitch two wanders left and back right, joining Drawstring where it has its bolt.

name: Sphincter Quits
beta: Follow the crack that slants rightward to the far end of a shelf, shuffle over, work a hairline fissure upward, and bear rightward for the exit. The original line instead leaves the left-hand ledge past a bolt and angles right to join the main way.
overview: A crack route starting at the far left edge of the face, with a thinner crack higher up.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: left edge of the face; slanting crack to a ledge, then a hairline crack

name: Violent Cooking
beta: Enter a corner that faces left, traverse leftward under a roof to reach a shelf, then keep going on the wall overhead, clipping two bolts.
overview: Climb a corner that faces left, traverse leftward beneath a roof to a ledge, then the face above with two bolts.

current.area_walk_in: Heading downhill northwest, passing either flank of Split Rock for roughly 50 yards, brings you to the lowest left toe of the massif. For the boulder routes, swing wide beyond Overbolted Rock keeping to its rightward flank, double back left, and scramble round the dome's northwest tip.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: toe of the massif at its lower left

name: Squid Vicious

name: Stan and Ollie

name: The Ledge

name: Step To The Left
beta: Think about gear placements carefully between the two bolts, and extend your clips, since drag builds up.
overview: A short two-bolt line that wants careful choices with natural gear. Expect heavy rope drag.

Take the left fork, which drops a little and then climbs again to the foot of the formation, where a tall bolted line stands straight ahead.

beta: A thin crack leads up toward a single bolt high on the route.

name: Strawberry Jam

name: Sucka Fish
beta: Pre-clip the opening bolt with a stick, or climb a neighboring route and clip it during the descent. The hard, bouldery sequence comes immediately off the ground.
overview: A short three-bolt line with a bouldery crux just off the ground.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.anchor: 2-bolt chains; also used by The Sea Cave

name: Sundance
beta: Pitch one follows an inside corner, then trends rightward to a short, strenuous lieback onto Log Ledge. Pitch two begins with a very hard move past a bolt, eases for a stretch, then traverses rightward to a protruding knob and then three further bolts to a crescent-shaped dihedral, which you abandon to the right at the earliest chance.
overview: Climbs the sunny face from the ground up to the far side of the high shelf, via a mid-height ledge and a crescent-shaped dihedral. The second pitch is praised highly, with bolt-protected face moves and a hard rightward traverse. The last pitch finishes up a crack.

current.area_walk_in: A climbers' trail starts opposite the tanks, drops to a seasonal stream, joins a paved lane to its end, then climbs a signed, rocky path to the base of the cliff.
current.location: Base of the face, beginning up an inside corner

name: Surprise
beta: Big holds next to a crack lead to a friction move trending left. Higher, a bolt guards a run of friction moves over a crystalline ridge, then a gentle lieback crack and a leftward traverse reach the foot of a trough, which has solid holds all the way to the summit.
overview: Thought to be the earliest big face line on this rock. It wanders up good holds next to a crack, then delicate friction over a crystal-studded ridge, and a gentle lieback crack. A traverse left leads to a wide trough that is followed to the top. The second pitch has a lengthy bold stretch without protection.

current.location: Beside a small fir at the middle of the foot of the wall

name: Exhibit A
beta: Work up and right along a ramp until partway along it, then continue vertically with a series of mantles, passing a bolt.
overview: Angle rightward along a ramp, then head directly upward on mantle moves beside the lone bolt.
